section_1.title: Introduction: The Challenge of Chaos (Duration: 45s)
section_1.content: Define turbulence not as disorder, but as a complex hierarchical cascade of energy. Introduce the Reynolds Number (Re) as the dimensionless ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces.
section_1.example: Visualize a calm river vs. a raging whitewater rapid; the transition point marks the breakdown of laminar flow into the chaotic swirl of turbulence.

section_2.title: The Kolmogorov Cascade: Mathematical Scaling (Duration: 1m 30s)
section_2.content: Explain Richardson's cascade (large eddies break into smaller ones). Introduce the Kolmogorov 1941 (K41) hypothesis. Present the Kolmogorov scale η (eta) as the threshold where viscous dissipation dominates.
section_2.example: Use an animation of a large hurricane spinning off smaller 'baby' cyclones, eventually dissipating into microscopic heat via friction.

section_3.title: The -5/3 Law: Spectral Analysis (Duration: 1m 30s)
section_3.content: Introduce the Energy Spectrum E(k) where k is the wavenumber. Explain why energy follows a power-law distribution. Present the graph of Log(E) vs Log(k) showing the steep -5/3 slope.
section_3.example: A musical analogy: large turbulent eddies are like low-frequency bass notes; small eddies are high-frequency treble notes, with the -5/3 law defining the 'mix' of the song.

section_4.title: Universal Constants & Dimensional Analysis (Duration: 1m)
section_4.content: Discuss the Kolmogorov constant (C), a universal value that emerges regardless of the fluid type. Use dimensional analysis (Buckingham Pi Theorem) to show how velocity fluctuations and dissipation rates determine this constant.
section_4.example: Imagine a mechanical 'Turbulence Robot' measuring water in a pipe vs. air in a wind tunnel; despite different fluids, the ratio of their kinetic energy decay remains constant.

section_5.title: Conclusion & Real-World Application (Duration: 15s)
section_5.content: Summarize how these mathematical structures allow us to simulate weather, design efficient aircraft, and understand stellar convection.
section_5.example: A final visual of a modern airplane wing design, showing how these fundamental constants prevent structural failure due to turbulent wind shear.
